what_its_for: This medicine is used to relieve moderate to severe pain. It contains two pain relievers that work together. Oxycodone is a strong opioid (narcotic) pain reliever that works in your brain to change how your body feels and responds to pain. Acetaminophen (the same ingredient in Tylenol) is a milder pain reliever that boosts the effect of oxycodone.
how_to_take: Take this medicine exactly as your doctor prescribed. Swallow the tablet or capsule whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food, but taking it with food may help if it upsets your stomach. Never crush, chew, break, or dissolve the tablet, as this can release too much medicine at once and cause serious harm or even death. Do not share this medicine with anyone else, even if they have similar pain. Sharing this medicine is illegal and dangerous.
dosing: Your doctor will set the right dose for you based on your pain level, weight, age, and health. A common adult dose is one or two tablets every 4 to 6 hours as needed for pain. Do not take more than your doctor tells you to. Very important: Do not take more than 4,000 mg of acetaminophen in one day from ALL sources (including Tylenol or cold medicines). Check all your other medicines for acetaminophen before taking this one. Taking too much acetaminophen can cause serious liver damage.
missed_dose: If you are taking this medicine on a regular schedule and you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose at the regular time. Never double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it in a secure, locked location out of reach of children and pets. Opioid medicines are a major cause of accidental overdose in children. When you no longer need this medicine, dispose of any leftover tablets safely. The best way is to use a medicine take-back program at your pharmacy or local police station. If no take-back program is available, flush unused tablets down the toilet to prevent misuse.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine. Alcohol mixed with oxycodone can cause dangerous drowsiness, slow breathing, and can be life-threatening. It also increases your risk of liver damage from the acetaminophen. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you, as it can cause serious drowsiness and dizziness. Avoid taking other medicines that contain acetaminophen (like Tylenol or many cold and flu products) without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first, to prevent accidentally taking too much. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, especially sleeping pills, anti-anxiety medicines, muscle relaxers, antidepressants, or any other opioid pain medicines, as combining them can be very dangerous.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you or someone you are with experiences: very slow, shallow, or stopped breathing; extreme sleepiness or cannot be woken up; blue or purple lips or fingertips; confusion or loss of consciousness; nausea, vomiting, or pain in the upper right stomach area (these could be signs of liver problems); yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); dark urine or pale stools; seizures; a fast or pounding heartbeat; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. If you suspect an overdose, call 911 immediately or call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222. Naloxone (Narcan) can reverse an opioid overdose — ask your pharmacist or doctor about getting it.
when_it_works: This medicine usually starts to relieve pain within 15 to 30 minutes after you take it. The pain relief typically lasts about 4 to 6 hours. It works best when taken at the first sign of pain rather than waiting until the pain is very severe.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): You may be more sensitive to the side effects, especially drowsiness, dizziness, constipation, and breathing problems. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose. Pregnant women: This medicine should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed and prescribed by your doctor. Taking it near the time of delivery can cause withdrawal symptoms in your newborn baby. Breastfeeding mothers: Oxycodone passes into breast milk and can harm your baby. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while taking this medicine. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children. Keep all opioid medicines safely locked away from children at all times. People with kidney or liver disease: You may need a lower dose or more frequent monitoring. Tell your doctor if you have any kidney or liver problems before starting this medicine.
